messages:
tessa: quick sketch — I want to propose adding 'Workload Classes' to our pricing surface. The idea: customers pick a class per-api-route (latency, batch, embed) and that maps to tier/add-ons and contract softcaps. Thinking this helps align unit economics w/ real workloads.
raul: sounds promising. want a quick taxonomy?
maria: +1. important for sales to explain why embeddings cost differently. can we map to existing add-ons (priority lane / burst credits)?
tessa: yes. draft mapping I had in mind: latency-sensitive -> higher per-token + priority lane, throughput-batch -> lower per-token + reserved slots, embed-only -> per-embedding unit pricing + caching credit. also a "mixed" flag for routes that toggle per-call.
kevin: any perf/runtime changes needed? continuous batching already covers throughput mode; priority lane implies queue differentiation. we can support with routing tags but engineering lift ~2 sprints.
eli: product launch criteria proposal: 1) docs + SDK flags + console UI for class assignment; 2) 3 internal benchmarks (chat latency, batched throughput, embedding QPS); 3) sales-ready contract language for softcaps/overage.
maria: + add a customer pilot with 2 customers (one startup with bursty traffic, one enterprise with steady high throughput). metrics: p50/p95 latency delta and cost-per-100k tokens.
raul: legal-bot — any red flags for adding route-level billing distinctions in contracts? especially around SLAs/fallbacks?
legal-bot: flagged items: must define "softcap" clearly (hours, triggers, smoothing), clarify fallback model (auto-failover to lower class?), and include clear termination/credit rules. suggest a short clause.
kevin: sample fallback behavior: if priority lane saturates, auto-fallback to throughput class with 95% of tokens at lower priority for next 5m. would need a config knob per-customer.
tessa: drafting clause for finance/legal review. rough text below: 
```
Softcap & Fallback: Customer-selected Workload Class determines routing priority. If selected class experiences sustained utilization above agreed softcap for 15 minutes, Redwood will route excess requests to the nearest compatible lower class. Customer will be notified and excess usage billed at the lower-class overage rate. Credits are available if sustained routing changes violate SLOs for >6 hours.
```
maria: can we add a one-time grace bucket for first 30 days of GA? helps adoption.
raul: sales impact: need clear examples for common patterns (search embeddings vs chat) and a pricing calculator snippet.
eli: rollout timeline suggestion: week 0 pilot + docs, week 2 narrow GA with opt-in, week 6 GA broadly. include a two-week free grace bucket for pilots.
kevin: engineering constraints note: per-route tagging + console UI + routing policy enforcement. estimate: 6 dev-weeks + 2 oncall readiness.
maria: metrics to validate before GA: cost-per-effective-request, customer satisfaction (NPS pilot), reduction in noisy-neighbor incidents.
tessa: ok I'll create PRD with mapping table, pilot customer list, and the legal clause. can someone own the pricing calc? @raul?
raul: I’ll take pricing calc. will mock workbook with 3 example customers.
eli: I can coordinate pilot ops + obs dashboards.
legal-bot: I'll queue a 48-hour review once PRD lands.
kevin: once PRD is up I’ll slack the eng-runtime team for implementation comms.
tessa: thanks all — will drop PRD link tomorrow. :pray:
